cells.tense: The questions are landing in real places now, and the asking is itself a practice.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Catch yourself turning something over past the point where it gives anything, and end the turning with a small act, same day, before asking again.
cells.core:
The pull toward what you actually want is working with the questions now, not against them. You ask a thing a second and third time and the light gets clearer for it, not dimmer, because the asking moves you toward what you want instead of postponing it. That is why you can usually tell whether a question took you somewhere.
Take a page and lay out what this last stretch has been teaching you about where you're pointed. Not a report of everything you read or watched — the shape that's actually forming. The pull will sometimes move faster than the asking, and this is where you catch that before a month slips by under questions that were only circling.
cells.sheetLine: Your questions are carrying you toward the light, not just around it.
cells.verb: asking your way toward the light, one question at a time
cells.place: the stretch of life where you can tell which direction you're steering by

cells.tense: The light is being lived in already, in a version of the life that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin one thing this week whose only job is being started — a project, a page, an afternoon — and don't ask it where it leads.
cells.core:
The pull has gone running past the questions, where you ask. Tomorrow's version of this life has been arrived at in the head, so today's asking feels slow and secondhand, and the questions get shorter while the visions of where they lead get brighter. There's real appetite in it; you can feel that while you plan. It's moving beyond what asks anything of you, and the asking is what walks you there.
A spark doesn't need directions to be yours. Start one thing whose only job is being started — a project, a page, one afternoon — and ask it for nothing beyond that. The light comes back in reach when your hands are in something small and true, and the questions start landing again because they have somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: The light is being lived in before you've walked there.
cells.verb: asking your way toward the light, one question at a time
cells.place: the stretch of life where you can tell which direction you're steering by

cells.tense: The questions were being asked in a room you've since left, and the light is behind you too.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Some evening, let a scene of where you'd like to be play out for ten minutes — pictures only, no decisions — then take the small step it suggests.
cells.core:
The asking has gone quiet and the light with it. You go through days of looking things over without any of it pointing anywhere, and the pull that used to tell you which direction was yours isn't in view. You still read, still consider; nothing is being steered by it, and you can feel the flatness in a morning without needing to name it.
Sleep works on what waking can't finish, and this is close to that. For one week, let a scene of where you'd like to be play out for ten minutes some evening — pictures, no decisions, no verdicts — then take the small step it suggests. Don't ask what the scene means or whether it's realistic; you're giving the pull something to move through. It finds your hands again before it finds your reasons.
cells.sheetLine: You keep asking. Nothing tells you which direction is yours.

cells.tense: The questions about where you're pointed are being asked in a voice others can hear, and you're saying it's just how you think.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Before settling a question about someone you live or work with, set out plainly what your choice gives them and what it costs them, then decide.
cells.core:
There's a pull in how you ask that people can hear. They ask what you're hoping for, and you say you're just trying to understand, and change the subject. That pull is at work through your questions; the way you describe it leaves out that it's a want with a direction, and the people asking can hear the difference, which is why they keep asking.
Some of that direction is visible to others, and their side of it counts. When a question about someone is about to be settled, put your answer's gift to them and its cost to them side by side on paper, then decide. The light stops sounding like a private thing you keep quiet about; it starts sounding like someone steering.
cells.sheetLine: Something is steering your questions, and you handle it as plain curiosity.
cells.verb: asking your way toward the light, one question at a time
